enonce.texte: Match the telephone expressions with their correct meanings. This exercise will help you remember key phrases used during phone calls.

questions.texte: Match each telephone expression with its correct meaning. Write the letter of the meaning next to the expression.

sousQuestions.texte: Hello, may I speak to [name]?
sousQuestions.reponse: A polite way to ask to talk to someone.

sousQuestions.texte: Who is calling, please?
Can I leave a message?
sousQuestions.reponse: Asking to pass information to someone who is not available.

sousQuestions.texte: I'll call you back later.
Could you repeat that, please?
sousQuestions.reponse: Politely asking someone to say something again.

enonce.texte:
Study the use of the imperative (giving orders or instructions) in telephone contexts. Then complete the sentences with the correct imperative form.

Reminder: The imperative uses the base form of the verb (without 'to'). For negative instructions, use 'Don't' + base verb.

questions.texte: Complete the sentences with the correct imperative form of the verb in parentheses.

sousQuestions.texte: (Call) _________ me when you arrive.
(Please / not / hang up) _________ yet!
(Wait) _________ a moment, I'll transfer you.
(Not / forget) _________ to call your mother.
(Take) _________ a message, please.

You want to ask someone to give you their phone number.
sousQuestions.reponse: Give me your phone number, please.

enonce.texte: In this exercise, you will practice leaving and taking phone messages. Read the situation and fill in the blanks with the correct expressions.

questions.texte: Read the telephone conversation and complete the message slip.

sousQuestions.texte:
Conversation:
Assistant: Good morning, ABC Company.
Caller: Good morning. Could I speak to Mr. Njoya, please?
Assistant: I'm sorry, he's in a meeting. Can I take a message?
Caller: Yes, please. This is Paul Tamo. He has a meeting tomorrow at 10 AM with the director. Please ask him to confirm.
Assistant: Sure, I'll give him the message.
Caller: Thank you. Goodbye.
Assistant: Goodbye.

Complete the message slip:

  • To: Mr. Njoya
  • From: _________
  • Message: _________
  • Action required: _________
sousQuestions.reponse:
To: Mr. Njoya
From: Paul Tamo
Message: You have a meeting tomorrow at 10 AM with the director. Please confirm.
Action required: Confirm the meeting.

questions.texte: You are the assistant. Your boss, Mrs. Mbella, is not here. Write down the message from the caller.

sousQuestions.texte:
Caller: Hello, this is Dr. Fouda from the hospital. I need to speak to Mrs. Mbella urgently. Her son is sick. I will call her back at 5 PM. Please tell her to wait for my call.

Write the message for Mrs. Mbella:
sousQuestions.reponse: Message for Mrs. Mbella: Dr. Fouda from the hospital called. He needs to speak to you urgently. Your son is sick. He will call you back at 5 PM. Please wait for his call.

intitule: Professional and Personal Phone Call Simulation

enonce.texte: Read the scenarios and write out the dialogue for each phone call. Use polite expressions, the imperative, and correct telephone vocabulary.

questions.texte: Scenario 1: You call your friend to invite them to a party. Your friend's mother answers.

sousQuestions.texte: Write the dialogue. You are the caller. Your friend's name is Marie.
sousQuestions.reponse:
You: Hello, good afternoon. May I speak to Marie, please?
Mother: Who is calling, please?
You: This is [your name], her friend.
Mother: One moment, please. I'll call her.
You: Thank you.

questions.texte: Scenario 2: You are a receptionist at a hotel. A customer calls to ask for information.

sousQuestions.texte: Write the dialogue. The caller asks about the price of a room and wants to make a reservation.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Receptionist: Good morning, Hotel Excellence. How may I help you?
Caller: Hello, I would like to know the price of a room for tonight.
Receptionist: A single room is 50,000 CFA francs per night.
Caller: OK, I would like to make a reservation.
Receptionist: Certainly. Can I have your name, please?
Caller: It's Mr. Ndi.
Receptionist: Thank you, Mr. Ndi. Your reservation is confirmed. We look forward to seeing you.
Caller: Thank you. Goodbye.
Receptionist: Goodbye.

enonce.texte: Read each problem and write a solution using appropriate telephone phrases. Use imperative forms and polite expressions.

questions.texte: You are in the middle of an important phone call and the line is very bad. You can't hear the caller well.

sousQuestions.texte: What do you say?
sousQuestions.reponse: I'm sorry, this line is very bad. Could you speak a little louder, please? Or: Could you call me back, please?

questions.texte: You are leaving an important message for your boss, but you realize you forgot to mention an important detail.

sousQuestions.texte: What do you do? Write your message.
sousQuestions.reponse: Hello, this is [your name]. I am calling to confirm the meeting at 3 PM. Also, please note that the client's name is Mr. Njoya. I will send you the address by email. Please call me if you have any questions.

questions.texte: You receive a call from an angry client who complains about your service.

sousQuestions.texte: Write your response to calm the client and solve the problem.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Client: I'm very upset! Your product is defective!
You: I'm very sorry to hear that, sir. Could you please tell me the problem? I will do my best to help you. Please give me your order number so I can check. I will call you back within the hour with a solution.
